rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence to exploit and maximum uncertainty across all design axes. The most informative first experiment is a minimal, well-understood baseline that establishes a reference performance level. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: PCA is a standard, low-risk dimensionality reduction; singleprofile avoids aggregation complexity; and no image or fusion components are involved. This gives a clean RNA-only reference that will be essential for later determining whether (a) learned RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) add value, (b) multiprofile aggregation helps, and (c) multimodal fusion actually improves over the single-modality baseline. Starting here reduces the risk of confounding implementation issues with design effects and anchors all subsequent comparisons.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 at 48.5% accuracy), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries any discriminative signal for this task. The very low baseline suggests either the task is inherently difficult or PCA on 2000 dims is an inadequate representation. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the simplest image-only configuration: it tests a fundamentally different information source (visual cellular morphology via a pretrained deep encoder) against the RNA-only baseline. This single experiment answers the highest-level design question—does the image modality provide useful signal at all?—before committing budget to the 30+ multimodal or more complex RNA-encoder variants. If image_only performs substantially better, it justifies investing in multimodal fusion and ViT variants; if it performs similarly poorly, the search should focus on improving RNA representations (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This is the most informative single experiment because it partitions the remaining configuration space into two very different strategic directions.

Evidence: RNA (pca_n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (resnet50) is weak at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether leveraging multiple cellular profiles with aggregation can improve the RNA baseline beyond the single-profile PCA result. This experiment (config_002) tests multiprofile + avgpool with the same pca_n2000 encoder, providing a clean, near-single-variable comparison to config_001 (only the profile/aggregation structure changes). It is the best use of the next budget slot because: (1) it isolates the effect of profile multiplicity and aggregation without confounding encoder choice, (2) avgpool is a low-risk, simple aggregator that is less likely to fail than a transformer with limited data, and (3) the result directly informs whether the multiprofile axis is worth further exploration (e.g., with scvi/scgpt encoders) or whether we should instead invest in encoder quality or multimodal fusion next.

Evidence: Multiprofile RNA with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA (config_001, acc=0.485), confirming that profile ordering and aggregation matter. Image-only resnet50 (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak, so RNA remains the primary signal. Question: Does transformer aggregation further improve over avgpool in the multiprofile RNA setting? This experiment (config_003) changes only the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer while holding rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed, giving a clean single-variable comparison against config_002. Why this is the best next step: It directly tests whether the ordering of multiple profiles carries additional signal beyond their mean, which determines whether we should invest further in more complex aggregation for downstream multimodal experiments. If transformer helps, it justifies transformer-based fusion in multimodal configs; if not, avgpool is sufficient and we can redirect budget toward RNA encoder choice or multimodal fusion.

Evidence: config_002 (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool) is the best result so far at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile+avgpool is a strong setting and that RNA dominates image (0.591 vs 0.208). The only RNA encoder tested is pca_n2000, leaving significant uncertainty about whether a learned encoder (scvi_n200) captures biological structure better than linear PCA. This experiment (config_005) changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding multiprofile+avgpool fixed, directly isolating the encoder effect against the known baseline of 0.591. Under a limited budget, this is the highest-information single-variable test: if scvi_n200 improves, it justifies investing in learned encoders for multimodal configs; if it does not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can redirect budget toward fusion/image questions with confidence.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (image_only resnet50: 0.208 vs rna_only: 0.485-0.650). Within RNA, multiprofile+avgpool is the best profile/aggregation setting (pca: 0.591 vs singleprofile: 0.485; avgpool: 0.591 vs transformer: 0.519), and scvi_n200 substantially outperforms pca_n2000 under identical settings (0.650 vs 0.591). This establishes a clear encoder ranking: scvi_n200 > pca_n2000. Question: Does scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, further improve on scvi_n200, or has encoder quality plateaued? config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) holds profile setting and aggregation at their known-best values, isolating the encoder effect. This is the best use of the next experiment because it directly extends the strongest evidence (encoder choice drives the largest observed gap), requires no new assumptions about aggregation or profile interactions, and will determine whether to invest remaining budget in encoder exploration or pivot toward testing image/multimodal contributions.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (best: scVI/multi/avgpool at 0.650), while the sole image test (ResNet50, single-profile) yielded only 0.208 accuracy, suggesting the image modality may carry little signal. However, ResNet50 is a relatively weak encoder; ViT-L (ImageNet-pretrained) is substantially more expressive and could extract features that ResNet50 missed. Uncertainty: We cannot yet determine whether the image modality is fundamentally uninformative for this task or simply poorly encoded. This experiment (config_014: image_only, multiprofile, ViT-L, avgpool) isolates the image encoder quality question while holding profile setting and aggregation at their known-best values (multiprofile + avgpool), avoiding confounds. If ViT-L still yields very low accuracy, we can confidently rule out the image modality and focus remaining budget on RNA-only optimization or fusion strategy. If it yields a meaningful signal, it justifies investing in multimodal experiments. This is the highest-information experiment available because it resolves a binary design question (is image useful at all?) that gates an entire family of ~36 multimodal configurations.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (best: scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool at 0.650 acc), while image-only models are weak (best: ViT-L multiprofile at 0.332). Within RNA, scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 > scgpt, multiprofile > singleprofile, and avgpool > transformer. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether adding image features to the best RNA configuration provides any complementary signal or merely adds noise. This experiment (config_030: multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) directly tests whether the simplest fusion (concat) of the best RNA setup with a modest image encoder improves over the 0.650 RNA-only baseline. It is the best next step because it extends the strongest known configuration along the single most important untested axis (fusion), uses the simplest fusion rule to isolate the effect of adding image information, and avoids changing multiple design choices simultaneously. If it fails to beat 0.650, it strongly argues against further multimodal exploration; if it succeeds, it justifies deeper fusion and image-encoder experiments.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200/multiprofile/avgpool (config_005) achieves 0.650 acc, while the only multimodal test (config_030: same RNA settings + resnet50/concat) drops to 0.632, suggesting the weak resnet50 image signal (image-only acc 0.208) adds noise rather than information. Meanwhile, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder yields substantially better image-only performance (0.332 vs 0.208). Question: Does a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) allow the multimodal model to match or exceed the RNA-only baseline? This experiment (config_036) is a clean single-variable comparison with config_030, changing only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while holding scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, and concat fusion constant. Why best next: It directly tests whether the image modality can contribute useful signal at all, which determines whether further multimodal exploration (fusion methods, transformer aggregation) is worthwhile or whether the budget should be redirected to RNA-only refinements. Under a limited budget, resolving whether multimodal is a viable direction is more informative than tuning fusion or aggregation within a likely unproductive regime.

The current best result is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat; acc=0.715). All multimodal experiments tested so far used concat fusion, so the effect of fusion strategy is completely unexplored. Config_037 changes only the fusion method from concat to weighted, holding all other settings identical to config_036. This is a clean single-variable experiment that directly tests whether a learned weighted combination of modalities can outperform simple concatenation. Given that the image modality alone is weak (best 0.33) while RNA is strong (0.65), the optimal weighting between modalities may differ substantially from an equal-weight concat, making this a high-information experiment. If weighted fusion improves performance, it confirms that modality importance is asymmetric and guides further tuning; if it does not, it confirms concat is sufficient and we can redirect budget toward other untested dimensions (e.g., transformer aggregation with scvi in multimodal).
